title: 呢: and you?
summary: Lets you bounce a question back or ask about someone else with a short phrase like 你呢？
structure: Person/Thing + 呢？ (asked right after someone has spoken)
explanation:
呢 at the end of a short question means "and you?" or "what about …?". First you say something about yourself, or hear an answer. Then you put a person or thing before 呢 to ask the same question about them. 我很好，你呢？ means "I'm fine, and you?"

It's easy to build. Take the person or thing you want to ask about and add 呢: 你呢？ 老师呢？ 你们呢？ You don't repeat the verb or the rest of the question. The sentence before it already tells the listener what you're asking.

Use it to keep a chat going. You can bounce a question back after you answer, or turn the talk to someone else. If nothing was said before it, 老师呢？ usually means "Where's the teacher?"

Don't mix it up with 吗. 吗 goes at the end of a full sentence and asks yes or no: 你好吗？ 呢 goes after a short phrase and leans on what was just said: 你呢？ Never use both together.

examples.en: I'm a teacher. What about you?
I like drinking tea. How about you?
I'm twenty this year. What about him?
Mom is at home. What about Dad?

mistakes.why: 吗 needs a full sentence before it, like 你好吗？ To bounce a question back with just 你, use 呢.
呢 always comes at the end, after the person or thing you're asking about.
Use only one question word at the end. 呢 already makes it a question, so don't add 吗.

why: 吗 needs a full sentence like 你好吗？. With just 你, use 呢.
Correct: 你呢？ bounces the question back: "and you?"
的 shows possession ("your") and can't end a question like this.
吧 is for suggestions or guesses, not for "and you?".

exercises.en: I'm a student. What about you?
why: 吗 asks a yes-no question about a full sentence. It doesn't work after a lone 你.
吧 makes a suggestion or guess. It can't mean "what about you?".
Correct: 你呢？ asks the same question back.
了 marks a finished action or a change. It doesn't make a "what about" question.

exercises.en: I like cats. How about you?
why: 呢 must come after the person: 你呢, not 呢你.
吗 needs a full sentence before it, like 你喜欢猫吗？
Question particles never come before the person, and 吗 also needs a full sentence. This option breaks both rules.
Correct: the person comes first, then 呢 at the end.

exercises.prompt: Which means "I'm busy today. What about you?"
why: Correct: 你呢？ asks "what about you?" after your own statement.
吗 can't follow a lone 你. It needs a full sentence like 你忙吗？
呢 goes at the end, after the person: 你呢.
吧 is for suggestions or guesses, not for bouncing a question back.
With 呢 you drop the verb. Say just 你呢, not 你是呢.
Don't use 呢 and 吗 together. One question particle is enough.
Correct: the first part sets the topic, and 你呢 asks the same about the listener.
呢 belongs at the very end, after the person: 你呢.

exercises.instruction: Shorten the second question with 呢.
why: Once you drop 好, 吗 can't stay. A short "and you?" needs 呢.
Correct: 你呢？ replaces the whole question 你好吗？
With 呢 you drop the repeated part and keep only the person: 你呢.
呢 goes after the person, not before.

exercises.instruction: Bounce the question back using 呢.
why: Don't keep the verb. 呢 follows just the person, so say 你呢.
Use only one question particle. 呢 and 吗 don't go together.
呢 doesn't turn a full sentence into a yes-no question. Either keep 你是老师吗？ or shorten it to 你呢？
Correct: 你呢？ means "and you?" and repeats nothing.

exercises.why: Put the person first and 呢 at the very end.
The whole phrase for the person comes first, and 呢 closes the question.
